description: West Bank green ID, Gaza ID, East Jerusalem blue permanent residency, and Israeli citizenship for '48 Palestinians. Four documents, four different sets of permitted movements, one people.
energy_note: Your rights arrive in a colour.

aspect: It decides who you can marry without consequence
description: Marrying across the tiers is the commonest way a family ends up living in two places, because the registry will not merge the two statuses.
energy_note: Falling in love with the wrong document.

aspect: And which hospital you may reach
description: The specialist centres are largely in East Jerusalem. A green ID cannot reach them without a permit, which means the referral and the permit are two separate processes with two separate failure modes.
energy_note: Referred to a hospital you are not allowed to enter.

aspect: Nobody chose their tier and everybody is judged by it
description: Within Palestinian society the tiers carry status, suspicion and resentment - the Jerusalemite with the blue card, the Gazan who cannot leave. The hierarchy is externally imposed and internally felt.
energy_note: Sorted into ranks by a filing system.

aspect: EXAMPLE - 340,000 people holding the document that is not a passport
description: Roughly 340,000 East Jerusalem Palestinians hold the Israeli laissez-passer, about 75% of all its holders. Most also hold Jordanian passports, but mostly temporary foreigner's passports rather than nationality passports. Residents were offered Israeli citizenship after the 1967 annexation and most declined for political reasons.
energy_note: Three hundred and forty thousand, sorted into a tier by one decision in 1967.
